one_liner: A customer-support chat agent for an online store (LangChain Deep Agents graph) that looks up orders, starts returns for delivered orders, and states the return policy.
system_prompt_excerpt:
system_prompt=(
        "You are a customer support agent for an online store. Use the order tools to "
        "look up orders and start returns, and never guess an order's status. Answer "
        "briefly."
    ),
hard_constraints: Use the order tools to look up orders and start returns, and never guess an order's status.

tools.name: look_up_order
tools.description: Look up an order by its id and report its item, status and any return.
tools.refuses: Unknown order_id (lookup is exact and case-sensitive) returns the ordinary string 'No order {order_id} exists.' and does not raise.
tools.effects: Read-only. Reads the in-memory _ORDERS dict. On success returns 'Order {id}: {item}, status {status}, return: {reason or none}.'

tools.name: start_return
tools.description: Start a return for a delivered order, giving the customer's reason.
tools.refuses: Returned as ordinary strings, never raised, checked in this order: unknown order -> 'No order {id} exists.'; status other than 'delivered' (e.g. A1002 shipped) -> 'Order {id} is {status} and cannot be returned yet.'; return already set -> 'Order {id} already has a return started.'. The reason is not validated (an empty string is accepted, and then the order's return is falsy, so look_up_order shows 'none' and a second start_return is allowed).
tools.effects: On success sets _ORDERS[order_id]['return'] = reason (in-memory, persists for the process lifetime) and returns 'Return started for order {id}: {reason}.'. The reason text is free text, taken from the customer or written by the agent. A later look_up_order shows the reason in 'return:'.

tools.name: return_policy
tools.effects: Read-only. Always returns 'Delivered items can be returned within 30 days for a full refund.' The 30 days are not checked against any order date.

orders.status: str (only 'delivered' and 'shipped' appear in the data; start_return requires 'delivered')
orders.return: str|None, the return reason once started, None otherwise

dependencies.name: in_memory_orders
dependencies.what: _ORDERS dict of three seeded orders (A1001 and A1003 delivered, A1002 shipped), all with no return.

runtime_dependencies.name: openai_compatible_chat_completions
runtime_dependencies.what: Chat-completions endpoint for the agent's LLM. OPENAI_BASE_URL sets the base URL, and unset means the OpenAI API. OPENAI_API_KEY is the key; the module imports with a placeholder 'unset' but a turn fails without a real key. OPENAI_MODEL defaults to vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash, a gateway model name.

tool_entrypoints.notes: Module-level function. It reads the module global _ORDERS, so no state argument.
Module-level function that mutates the module global _ORDERS.

refusal_signature: Refusals are ordinary returned strings, not exceptions. They are 'No order {id} exists.', 'Order {id} is {status} and cannot be returned yet.', and 'Order {id} already has a return started.'. Success strings begin 'Order {id}: ' (look_up_order), 'Return started for order ' (start_return), and 'Delivered items can be returned' (return_policy).

data_store.configured_by: Hardcoded module-level dict _ORDERS in agent.py. There is no connection setting. State is mutated in memory by start_return and resets on process restart.

real_use_cases: Look up an order by id and report its item, status and any return on it.
Start a return for a delivered order with the customer's reason.
Refuse to start a return for an order that has not been delivered, or that already has a return started.
Tell the customer the store's return policy.
Report that an order id does not exist rather than guessing its status.
caller_identity: The agent never identifies the person. No login, number or account is used. The customer supplies an order id in the conversation, and any order id works for any caller.
notes: Single agent, one graph: langgraph.json maps 'support' to ./agent.py:graph, a deepagents create_deep_agent graph built once at import. The agent folder has no Dockerfile or Compose file, so the user's note about a standalone Dockerfile does not apply, and native Python 3.12 is the deployment declared. ASSUMPTION, NOT PROVEN IN THE AGENT'S SOURCE: the folder ships no HTTP server, agent_callback or command entrypoint. The README says only that the kit's own LangGraph adapter loads agent.py:graph and sends each turn the whole conversation as `messages`, replying with the last message's text. The runtime command and interface declared here (`langgraph dev` on port 2024, stateless POST /runs/wait with assistant_id 'support', reply read from messages.-1.content, health /ok) come from the standard LangGraph server convention applied to langgraph.json. `langgraph-cli` (with the inmem extra) is NOT in requirements.txt and would have to be installed in the runtime, and the declared interface has not been verified by a readiness check. If it fails, the kit's adapter entrypoint should replace it. Deep Agents' built-in tools (filesystem, planning todos, sub-agent task) are added by the framework and are not traced, so they are not listed as tools. Tool failures never raise, so a refusal is only visible in the returned string. The 'return' key is falsy for an empty reason, which lets a second return be started on that order. Order lookup is case-sensitive. Order state is process-global and not per conversation, so a return started in one conversation persists into later ones in the same process.
open_questions: The chat ingress is assumed to be `langgraph dev` plus POST /runs/wait because the source has no ingress of its own. Confirm this, or give the kit adapter's real entrypoint.
langgraph-cli is not in requirements.txt, so how should it be installed in the runtime?
Which model endpoint and key will be supplied (OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL)? The default model name is a gateway name that the OpenAI API does not accept.
